utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, and good morning, Colonel Landry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers [Cont'd]:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, I take it that most of your written work with the ECMM was carried out in the English language; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe that you testified in French in the Blaskic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You do not speak Croatian yourself, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during your tour of duty with the ECMM, you were exclusively dependent upon interpreters to gain an understanding of what your Croatian interlocutors were saying; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, you have an exclusively military background, correct, in the Canadian army?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've never commanded troops in combat, though, have you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you kept contemporaneous notebooks of your experiences in Central Bosnia from March to August of 1993; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fair to say, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you used those to refresh your recollection in order to prepare for your testimony yesterday and today?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe, sir, that the investigators that work for the Prosecution spent just about a week with you in 1996, meeting with you and going over your personal archives. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you let them see whatever they wanted to see, including your notebooks; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't see everything that I had. They had to ask for exactly specific items or specific periods, and then they looked at what I had covering those periods. But I was always there with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. But whatever they asked for, you provided; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the witness statement that you gave and signed on August the 9th, 1996, you referred to a significant number of reports that were prepared. We have requested those, but they have not been provided to us. One of them is listed on page 3. It's a list of significant officials of the government of Herceg-Bosna. Do you recall that list at all?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I definitely recall having in my possession copies of certain Herceg-Bosna documents, yes, but I don't know if they are exactly the same as the one that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. It would be fair to say, though, that you don't have with you today the document that contained the list of the significant officials of Herceg-Bosna that's referred to on page 3 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have them with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. You actually arrived in Central Bosnia, Colonel Landry, I believe, in early March of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you arrived, the British Battalion component of the UNPROFOR forces had responsibility for the Vitez/Busovaca area; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Canadian Battalion had responsibility for the Kiseljak area?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Visoko/Kiseljak, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the French Battalion had responsibility for the Kakanj area; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you left Central Bosnia or left your duties as the then deputy head of the RC Zenica on August the 24th of 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think that you were actually first appointed to perform duties with the ECMM attached to the RC Zenica on March the 6th of 1993. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, Mr. Sayers, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as a monitor?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Maybe it's a day or so before, because --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About that, early March?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it would be fair to say that most of your colleagues, the ECMM monitors who were drawn from various armed forces around the world, had very limited knowledge about the countries that comprised the former Yugoslavia, including the relatively new Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Initially, sir, when you arrived in Zagreb to prepare yourself for taking up your duties, you were briefed for just a couple of days at the headquarters of the ECMM in Zagreb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right. But I must say, though, that I had been receiving briefing back in my own country on that conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you undertake any studies yourself of the political structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina or its history?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following my stay with the ECMM, I underwent a postgraduate programme, and my thesis was on Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before that time, would it be fair to say that you knew very little, if any, about --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew very little except what -- the briefing that I had received in my own headquarters in Ottawa, and then the briefing that I received at Zagreb, and then the briefing that I received at RC Zenica when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, part of your briefing included the ECMM's popular wisdom that the HVO was controlled by the Croatian army in Zagreb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the beginning. I must say that it was mentioned that there was definitely a link between the Croatian army and HVO to the effect that, when I arrived, I was told that the Croatian army was controlling the HVO. It was not put to me in those words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, part of the briefing materials that were shown to you said that the Croatian Defence Council, HVO, is believed to be controlled by the Croatian army from Zagreb. And I'm just reading from your Blaskic testimony.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying, it's believed to be controlled, but that doesn't say that it was controlled by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that fell into the category of so-called unconfirmed information, as opposed to confirmed information, right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's the reason, for example, that throughout the spring that we received different communication from Zagreb trying to prove evidence that in fact there was HV forces within Bosnia-Herzegovina, so eventually to try to confirm this unconfirmed statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there is a strong distinction between confirmed and unconfirmed information or reporting within the ECMM, right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the extent of HV involvement, if any, was never confirmed during your tour of duty, was it?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said yesterday. I said yesterday that we had evidence that in the area of Prozor, Jablanica, that we have seen and I had personally seen logistic equipment coming from the HV, which were then reported by some military representative of the HV as being the fact that they had military logistic equipment in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to engage in conversation with any of the drivers of these alleged HV vehicles?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't speak to any HVO forces to determine whether these were HV troops; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't speak to any HV troops to determine that they were in fact HV troops? Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is fair to say, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all we have is your deductions based upon a visual sighting?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's more than that. It's -- you must realise that the way that information is being collected, okay, and the way that we more or less try to confirm information is not just based on one source but based on multiple sources. So all I have been saying is that we had multiple reports that people had seen equipment with appellation or with signatures, okay, that on those equipment that were not common to HV forces, that were more or less common to -- sorry, that were not common to HVO forces, but were common to HV forces. And all I said is that in addition to that, I personally saw that type of vehicle with the same signature. And then to me, one plus one, then one, that, yes, there was definitely HV equipment in the area of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's just turn for a minute to your position as a monitor, sir. Newcomers always were required to spend a short time as monitors in the field; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it's true that the RC Zenica, initially anyway, was responsible for a vast amount of territory through the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as soon as you arrived in Zenica, you were appointed to be the head of the Busovaca Joint Commission; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily correct. I became the head of the Busovaca Joint Commission. You must realise that we were three military -- or three observers on that commission, and as the new kid on the block, I was one of the monitors on that commission. And then eventually I came to be the head of the Busovaca Joint Commission. But I was not at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you became -- I think you held a position with the Busovaca Joint Commission from the initiation of your duties until the commission was --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically until, I would say, the end of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I believe the Busovaca Joint Commission or the Vitez Joint Commission, as it was then known, was phased out of existence on April the 22nd, as part of the ceasefire agreement, and then became part of the joint commission headquartered in Travnik; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After April the 22nd, sir, most of your work was done in your own office, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no. I became then the chief of operation, and I then became, as you've said earlier, the deputy head. But one of my responsibilities was to keep in touch with the numerous CC that RC Zenica had. Which means that I did have the occasion on numerous -- yes, on numerous occasion to travel at length, to visit Tuzla and to visit all the other, Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, and Mostar, all the other CC that we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But after April the 22nd, your duties became more national --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in quality rather than original --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were also the officer in charge of intelligence, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not -- I never was the officer in charge of intelligence. All I have said is that I have a background in intelligence, because we didn't have this function within the RC Zenica, and I don't think that we had any such posts within the ECMM. We had people that were working in operation, collecting information, but as such, the word "intelligence" was never used to my --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, on pages 7586 and 7587 of the Blaskic testimony that you gave two years ago, you said, "I myself was an officer in charge of intelligence."

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I went through this transcript, and I must say that one of the reasons why I have decided to do it this time in English was that the translation, to my point of view, was not to its best. All I said was that I was trained as an intelligence officer, but I don't recall receiving any specific information that I was to be appointed within RC Zenica as an intelligence officer. And again, I am very strong on it; that is, I do not recall seeing any posts within all of the ECMM where people were strictly appointed as an intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your service on the Busovaca Joint Commission was concluded, it's true, isn't it, that you did a stint as an ECMM team leader with Dieter Schellschmidt and were responsible for Zenica, Vitez, Kiseljak, Kacuni, and Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Dieter Schellsmidt was with me on the Busovaca Joint Commission. And one of the things that we did together is that as we were going further down the chain of command to implement the ceasefire, which the Busovaca Joint Commission had to overlook, we had to work extensively on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Landry, if you don't mind, we'll get along a lot quicker if you just answer that question. You did a stint as an ECMM team leader with Mr. Schellsmidt for about 15 days after you ceased your duties on the Busovaca Joint Commission?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The point that I just wanted to mention to you was this was part of the Busovaca Joint Commission; it was not outside of the Busovaca Joint Commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Was the 15-day stint that you spent in that slot before you left the Busovaca Joint Commission or after?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was during the Busovaca Joint Commission, the end, towards the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you were appointed assistant operations officer at RC Zenica in the second week of May of 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was then appointed chief of ops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you held that position until the end of July?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you became deputy head of the RC Zenica, a position that you occupied for about three weeks; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it true to say that when you arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you found a very unusual situation on the ground? For example, in villages, the belligerents had basically grouped themselves within various municipalities and even within various villages and were basically keeping surveillance on each other about 24 hours a day?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was a very tense and odd situation, that sort of ethnic polarisation; wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, would you agree that you detected a deep-rooted animosity between the warring parties, with much of the population, if not virtually all of it, under arms at that time?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would quote slightly different the last part of your statement. But overall, I would say "yes".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever read the fifth periodic report prepared by the United Nations Commission on Human Rights on the 17th of November, 1993? I was just reading from that, sir, which made the observation that much of the country -- this is in paragraph 12 on page 4 of the report. "Much of the country is under arms and the population is increasingly polarised."

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall reading that document, but I would tend to more or less agree with what's written there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just a few more questions on the situation as you found it when you first arrived. It's true that in the spring of 1993, not many government institutions were actually working, were they?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look at the central government first and then the municipal institutions. The central government was actually cut off and surrounded by forces of the Bosnian Serb army; would you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore the central government had virtually no communication with the various municipalities in the outlying areas; would you agree with that too, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No communication in the formal way of being able to take the telephone and contact them. The communications were done through a more lengthy process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But basically the government simply wasn't working, was it, the central government?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was something which was working, because one way or the other, there was information that was being passed through, and eventually there was movement of troops and there were changes of attitude. But it was more or less in the much more slower process, due to the situation that you depicted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in the Blaskic case a couple of years ago, sir, you said that at that time there were not many institutions operating in Central Bosnia, the police were not terribly active, there was no justice system in place. That's page 7474. And then you went on to make the observation that the two military chiefs, one on the HVO side, one on the ABiH side, were, for all practical purposes, to use your words, the authority par excellence which predominated at the time?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you still agree with that testimony that you gave two years ago?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. May I say something more than just "yes", because I think that this type of question required to specify a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Colonel, it's a matter for us to decide what is said here, not for counsel. If you can deal with the matter -- if you want to expand an answer, do. But if you would bear in mind that we'll finish more quickly if you simply say "yes" or "no". But if you want to expand something, do. Also bear in mind that prosecuting counsel can re-examine on any matter which he thinks important which you haven't clarified. But would you like to clarify that last answer?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I'll try to be very brief. Yes, you're right, and the reason why I said that is that everything was being governed by whoever was wearing a uniform, and that's what I meant. And at that time, it appears very obvious to me that the government was able to govern, okay, whatever side, through the use of their military forces, because the civilian police, we could not see if it was civilian police or military police. So that's what I meant by that, is that the country or those areas were being governed by -- through the military forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you first arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you also said, on page 7486 in Blaskic, that it was clear to you that the country was wracked by an ethnic conflict, that Muslims detested the Catholics, and vice versa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not put it in this way. That's what probably I was led to believe by the briefing that I received, but I think that yesterday and throughout my deposition on Blaskic, I illustrated that I was then led to believe that the animosity was not really coming from the bottom up but was more or less imposed from the top to bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you did say, sir, that when you arrived -- you say this on lines 19 through 23 of page 7486: "It should be said that when I arrived in Bosnian territory, I already had an understanding of the situation. I was convinced that we were facing an ethnic conflict, that the Catholics detested the Muslims, and vice versa." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say, and again all I can say, I didn't read that script before, I was never given a copy of how my deposition in English was reflected, but all I can remember is that, yes, that's what I was told when I arrived in Bosnia, that there was an ethnic conflict. But later on, okay, I more or less slightly changed and amended this version through different experiences that I had and which I was able to provide, as evidenced throughout my statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please slow down, because it is very difficult for the interpreters to follow, and likewise to listen to the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You've been told to slow down a little. Actually, I say "we". I've been told to slow down a little, and I'll do my best to do that. Would you agree, Colonel Landry, that it was very difficult, when you were in Central Bosnia, to distinguish between a regular soldier, a militia member, police officers, and even civilians, because essentially everybody was in uniform?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And both the HVO and the ABiH used military and regular police, and it was difficult to distinguish between civilian and military police. You would agree with that too; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would also agree that there were horrible stories of atrocities, murders and so on on both sides throughout your time in the country; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You would also agree, sir, that the presence or absence of a uniform tells us very little about whether the wearer was a soldier or not, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave some important statistics, Colonel Landry, in the Blaskic case. You said that of a population of about 4,4 million in August of 1993 when you left, about 2,2 million of the population or 50 per cent consisted of displaced persons. Is that still your view today after the studies that --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's still my view, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's true that the population of Zenica practically doubled as a result of the arrival of refugees and displaced persons from various areas in the spring of 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same is true of Busovaca and Vitez, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please make pauses between answer and question? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... weekly summary, and we can put it on the ELMO, if you wish, dated the 20th or the 26th of June, 1993, which makes the observation that in Kakanj, Vares, Kiseljak, and Vitez, the displaced persons situation had reached almost critical levels. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it is something that I have reported, yes, I would definitely think that what I reported was exactly what I was seeing and reading in the situation at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Let me turn your attention first to the area with which you were first associated, the Busovaca area. It's true that you arrived after the conclusion of the fighting, the outbreak of fighting in January, and that the main supply route from Busovaca to Kiseljak had been cut off by ABiH forces from the 333rd Mountain Brigade and as well as others between the villages of Kacuni and Bilalovac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Umm-hmm, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at no time after your arrival, as far as you're aware, or before the end of the war was the HVO ever able to muster the military strength to re-establish control over the main supply routes between Busovaca and Kiseljak, was it?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the Busovaca Joint Commission, sir, had been established before your arrival?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was established as a joint forum where the parties involved in the fighting could air their differences, raise contentious issues, to be resolved through negotiations instead of armed conflict; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but with the aim of implementing the ceasefire agreement that had been signed by both military commanders of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And the ceasefire agreements, I believe, were signed -- and I believe you've seen them -- by Colonel Blaskic and by General Hadzihasanovic and countersigned by Ambassador Thebault and Colonel Stewart or Lieutenant-Colonel Stewart from BritBat; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic was never involved at any time in those ceasefire negotiations, as far as you were aware, was he?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly, probably not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or even indirectly? You don't have any knowledge whatsoever of his involvement in those negotiations, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no involvement, yes, in those negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the structure of the Busovaca Joint Commission, as I understand it, consisted at the upper echelon of a coordination committee that met once per month; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that consisted of three to six UNPROFOR representatives, HVO and ABiH representatives, as well and ECMM representatives; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Kordic was never on that coordination committee, was he?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask the usher to put one page from Exhibit D23/1 on the ELMO, and that might refresh your recollection. Mr. Usher, I have that here. This page, Annex A. Yes. All right, sir. As we can see, this is a document that shows the organisation of the joint coordination commission, and it shows the coordination committee consisting of the commanding officer of BritBat, the chairman of the ECMM, as well as the commanders of variously the 3rd Corps and the HVO central command; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would agree that Mr. Kordic never sat on the coordination committee, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, it's true that Mr. Kordic never attended a single meeting of the Busovaca Joint Commission while you were its head, or while you were a member; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The committee actually met every day, didn't it, or tried to? Not the coordination committee, the actual Busovaca --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The working group, yes. On a daily basis, from eight till six, sometimes seven days a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand it, the working group -- the group representatives with whom you liaised principally were Colonel Merdan for the Muslim forces, and Mr. Nakic for the Croat forces?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in addition to that, they were being accompanied by two other staff officers from their headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the plan was for Colonel Merdan to report up his chain of command regarding incidents and complaints, and for Mr. Nakic to do the same to his chain of command; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both sides regularly made complaints of breaches of International Humanitarian Law against each other. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way that the whole process started, by letting both sides to provide their brief, their protests, and then we were investigating that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then investigative groups would be formed, go out during the day to investigate the complaints, and then report back at night; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. At night or the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were a member of the Busovaca Joint Commission, would it be fair to say that you never asked Mr. Kordic to attend a single meeting of that institution?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I believe, sir, that the -- initially set up in Busovaca, the Busovaca Joint Commission moved to Vitez in the last week of March, 1993, and changed its name as a result. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave some testimony about the village of Skradno, sir, and the investigations that you performed concerning complaints about harassment of Muslim citizens in that town. The same kinds of complaints were being made by Croats about harassment of Croat citizens in other little villages. Wouldn't that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've just described that the way that this commission was supposed to work, envisaged complaints being passed up the military chain of command, and then, within a reasonable amount of time, improvements were supposed to have been put in place by the military commanders; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But I must say too, at certain times the municipality, which we had to do, were being involved too. So I recall having meetings with the mayor or representatives of mayors trying to eventually make sure that the ceasefire agreement was being then implemented, not just by the military, but by getting the community involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You took active steps to ensure that the instructions from the military leadership filtered down to the subordinate commanders and the civilian government members in Busovaca, for example, or Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after your investigations about the complaints of harassment of Muslim citizens in Skradno, things did improve there, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, because I kept going there on numerous occasion. What did improve, though, is the fact that since we were going there at random, naturally, they were not any longer -- they knew that they could not any longer keep on doing the type of thing that they were doing. But the situation never really improved. Okay --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said on page 7608 of your April the 21st, 1998 testimony in Blaskic, as follows, when you first reported the complaints about Skradno. "I told them, the HVO, the first time I went there that the people had been forced to line up against the walls of their houses and go through a mock execution. As far as I can remember, those incidents did not take place again. Therefore, for me there was already some improvement. It was clear that some of the information had reached there." So what you are saying, sir, that the Busovaca Joint Commission was doing, what it was really envisaged to do, and that was to try to diffuse some of the tensions that had been build up in the local towns and villages?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Diffuse by at least being allowed to have a regular presence on the ground so that in fact people would know that they could not keep doing what they were doing, because it would be reported. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did see some improvement in Skradno?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the line that you just mentioned, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to the Vance-Owen Plan about which you gave testimony. This was a plan that was developed by the International Community to try to bring peace to this troubled region; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the plan was fully supported by the International Community; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croats were the first to sign full acceptance of all portions of the plan; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say the Croat, you mean the Bosniak Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bosniak Croat contingent, yes. And then ultimately, I believe, the Muslims --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: 23rd of March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And then, I believe, the Bosnian Serbs initially accepted the plan, except to ratification by the Republika Srpska assembly in Pale, and then the Pale assembly refused to ratify the plan; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you yourself never heard that the Croats had ever presented any kind of an ultimatum to the Muslim side in connection with the implementation of this plan; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, sir, you never heard of any kind of an ultimatum from Colonel Blaskic, did you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or from any other source with whom you were dealing in the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except that later on we got copies of those correspondence between -- copy of correspondence of Mate Boban about the fact that this 15 of April was to be a kind of a special date as far as the full implementation of the Vance Owen, but never to the effect that we were fully aware of what was the additional deals. We knew that something else was going on, because if you look at the Vance-Owen Plan, you will realise that the Vance-Owen Plan left some latitude to be further settled down by the Muslims, and the Bosniak Muslims, and the Bosniak Croats. For example, the way that the whole military structure would be further organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But in your functions as a prominent ECMM monitor responsible for the Vitez-Busovaca region on the ground, you never heard of any such ultimatum while you were in the field, so to speak, did you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I mean, one of the tasks that the ECMM received upon this plan was to facilitate its implementation. So we received numerous briefing on the Vance-Owen Plan and, as I said, I mean, I have recollection of seeing the paper signed by Mr. Mate Boban about this 15 of April. And I think that I had the copy of those documents in my possession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just suggest to you, sir, that on page 7735 of the Blaskic testimony that you gave, Judge Shahabuddeen asked you whether you were ever aware of the issue of an ultimatum having been issued by the Croatian side to the Muslim side requiring implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan by the 15th of April. And your answer was, "When we were on the ground, I was not given that type of information. The only thing that I can remember is, I believe, that the Muslims or Izetbegovic had signed the Vance-Owen Plan at the end of April, or at least he had let it be understood that he had agreed with the implementation or at least the principles of the Vance-Owen Plan."

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And you are not saying anything differently today?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Now, I wonder if you could be shown Exhibits Z571.1 and Z571.3, which was identified during the direct examination. Just give them to the witness, if you wouldn't mind. Exhibit 571.3, sir, was something that is entitled "Annex 4" and in agreement on interim arrangements. Do you know whether this was actually ever incorporated into the Vance-Owen Plan itself?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the added page dated 25 of March? Is that what -- because I have two documents here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 571.3 is the exhibit that I want you to look at, the exhibit you were shown by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: And again your question is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether this document was actually made a part of the final version of the Vance-Owen Plan, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to go through it to see exactly what it is. All I can say is that we had a copy of the Vance-Owen Plan, and if it is the Vance-Owen Plan, I would say yes, we had it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you a document that has in fact been identified by the parties in this case as a copy of the Vance-Owen Plan. It should be Exhibit 571.1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an exhibit that was tendered yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This was tendered several months ago. I have an extra copy here, if you need it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel Landry. If you just take a look at the exhibit that's been put before you. Do you recognise this as a copy of what has been known as the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the official way to publish the document. But I must say, though, that in the field, okay, it's more or less a copy that -- that you showed me that we received in our RC Zenica. So I was never able to get this type of official document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you just turn to page 137, sir, which deals with interim provincial governments.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As I understand it, sir, the arrangement was for each province, each of the ten provinces or cantons, to have first a governor that would be appointed by the majority ethnic component of the population, then a vice-governor appointed by the next most numerous ethnic component of the population, and then ten other members on an interim provincial government, consisting of a mixture of the three constituent peoples: Muslims, Croats, and Serbs. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is fair to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you just turn to the next page. Actually, if you turn to page 139, sir. Province 10 is dealt with, and it's fairly easy to understand. Province 10 has as its capital Travnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The governor was to be nominated by party A, which is the Croats, the Croat party, the HDZ BiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The vice-governor was to be nominated by the Muslim party, the SDA; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then five members of the provincial -- the ten member provincial government were to be nominated by the SDA, four by the HDZ BiH, and one by the Serbian party, SDS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what's written there, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And is that what you were informing the Muslims and the HVO in connection with your efforts to educate the locals about the components of the Vance-Owen Plan? That's the governmental structure that was envisaged and that was what you were promulgating on behalf of the ECMM; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, that's relatively easy to understand, sir, isn't it? That looks like, to me, a balanced governance structure with power pretty much equally shared between Croats and Muslims in Travnicka province, province number 10. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. May I make just one comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I'm not quite sure. Where are we going here? What is the purpose of these questions, Mr. Sayers? Will you assist us?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The purpose of the questions was, Mr. President, just to underscore the fact that the Vance-Owen Plan always set out a fairly simple governance structure and always envisaged a sharing of power between Croats and Muslims. And I am not exactly sure how Colonel Landry or his colleagues at the ECMM addressed the contentions that somehow the Vance-Owen Plan was supposed to create ethnically homogeneous provinces, because clearly it was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Colonel, perhaps you would like to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very easily. We never argue about the nature of the Vance-Owen Plan. What we said was the interpretation of it. For example, if I go to Travnik, it was very obvious for us that as soon as the Vance-Owen Plan had been agreed, it was much more tension, okay, that arise, and as soon as Travnik had been decided as to be the capital of that province, then suddenly the local authority, which happened to be Muslim, were being displaced, were being ousted out, and then were being replaced by other Croat representatives which have not been legally elected. And it appears to us that as this was happening, there was much more intense ethnic discrimination taking place, which we had the feeling that the Muslims were being forced out and that which we had -- which ECMM had at the same time received a lot of pressure by the HVO and the Bosniak Croat authorities to make sure or to force us to allow the displacement of the Croats that were living in Zenica to move to Province 10. That's all we were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sayers, I should like to ask Colonel Landry, does it transpire from your analysis of the Vance-Owen Plan and does it therefore transpire that there would be some cantons which would be predominantly Croat or Bosniak Croat, if one might call them that way, and others which would be predominantly Bosniak Muslim?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Sayers, I do not really think it would be worth going into detail about this partition, because we know about that. The problem is how the plan was received and if it was received as Colonel Landry tells us, and therefore those were the consequences of it. And to go into various technicalities of the Vance-Owen Plan, I do not know if we have to go there. Perhaps, of course, it is of interest to people with a legal education, but otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I stand justly upbraided, Your Honour, and I think we'll move on smartly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one question, sir. Did you ever discuss the details of the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan with any of the Bosnian Croat political leadership in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done basically by Ambassador Thebault. Okay, you must realise that we had many things to do, and one of the things that we were attempting to do was to voice this Vance-Owen Plan to the locals, okay, and Ambassador Thebault was the one more or less taking care of the very senior level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you yourself had no such discussions with the leadership of the Bosnian Croats in --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Besides the leadership at the local level and some municipalities, as I said. I did meet with the mayor at that level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never discussed it, though, with Mr. Kordic, for example, did you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that, except that once, though, I did pay a visit to one of the other very senior members of the Croat government, okay, near Mostar. I have a recollection of paying him a visit, and we did, in fact, talk about the Vance-Owen Plan. This was later on, maybe May or June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's in Herzegovina, though; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never discussed it with Mr. Kordic, though, or any other Croat political leader in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly, you never discussed it with Colonel Blaskic, did you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to another subject, the chain of command in the HVO. Were you aware that the supreme commander of the armed forces of the HVO throughout your tour of duty, sir, was the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume, as I said yesterday. I mean the military has to answer to the government, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you understood that Mr. Boban was the president of the so-called HZ HB, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that there was a separate institution known as the presidency, quite apart from the president? No? All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. It's true also that the general staff of the HVO and its headquarters was located in Mostar or just outside; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were with the ECMM, Colonel, the commander in chief was Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the Blaskic case, you stated that you were of the impression that HVO troops generally responded and reacted to the chain of command, and I take it that's your view today as well.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, throughout your tour of duty for six months in Central Bosnia, there is absolutely no doubt at all that it was Colonel Blaskic who was the military commander of HVO armed forces in Central Bosnia, is there?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, I think in your statement to the Prosecution's investigators a number of years ago, you said that he was definitely the HVO military commander throughout your tour, and you still think that way today; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, Colonel Blaskic displayed to you a great deal of knowledge about his brigade commanders and the disposition of the forces under his command; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's fair to say, but assuming too that they were having problems with control of certain elements and, yes, considering the situation and, as I said yesterday, the fact that they were not fully a professional army, we realised that there was a certain element of control at time to time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you articulated your view, I believe, on direct examination, that Colonel Blaskic, as the military commander of the forces in his area of responsibility, had the obligation to ensure that all of the troops under his command properly responded to his authority; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also are of the view that it's simply not possible to believe that he did not have an exercise of full control over all of the troops under his command; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except the point that I just made a few minutes regarding the fact that they didn't have a professional army and they didn't have all the necessary tools of communication too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In fact, you were asked by Judge Riad two years ago, at page 7725 of your testimony, whether Colonel Blaskic was the uncontested commander of all HVO forces in Central Bosnia, and you said that's exactly what he was; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, going down to the next level, Colonel, the brigade commands, it's true that the HVO's military organisation envisaged a system of municipality or territorially-based brigades with their soldiers or forces drawn from the local environs; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And beneath the brigades, they were organised into satnijas or companies, each commanded by a company commander who reported to the brigade --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Company commander or battalion commander sometime, depending on the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And then the brigade commanders reported up the chain of command to the Operative Zone commander, Colonel Blaskic; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, in turn, reported to his CO, his commanding officer, Brigadier Petkovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you gave some testimony about the Busovaca brigade commander, Dusko Grubesic. He was the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade in that town; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recall him as being the Busovaca Brigade commander on the HVO side, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. There's no question that he was the local HVO commander in Busovaca, according to your recollection; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was definitely the brigade commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've described, in graphic terms, how events gradually began to accelerate out of control in April of 1993. I wonder if I could just ask the usher to show you a document that was marked as Exhibit D146/1, which is an ECMM special report dated April the 7th, 1993. In paragraph 1, sir, the comment is made that: "The coordination committee meeting of the Busovaca Joint Commission was held today, April the 7th, 1993, in the FrenchBat location at Kakanj due to the HVO representatives' high concern about their security after blackmail sent during the last days by Muslim hard-liners at Zenica." Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have -- I know that we had a lot of problems in Kakanj eventually during my stay and I had to intervene on numerous occasions, so I would tend to say, yes, that could be part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This comment, though, sir, makes the observation that the threats had been received from Muslim hard-liners in the city of Zenica and that the meeting had to be convened in Kakanj due to the concerns expressed by the HVO representatives for their safety. Do you have a recollection of this incident or not?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'm through with that. Even though your perception was that in places like Travnik, sir, tensions were beginning to rise at the beginning of April, it's true, isn't it, that the local commanders in Busovaca actually met and reached agreement on April the 8th and 9th, 1993, for things such as filling in of fortifications like trenches; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was Commander Grubesic from the HVO and Commander Dvevad Mekic from the 333rd Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had been able to get written -- finally written orders two months after the ceasefire had been agreed by their commander, and that's the document that I needed to have the local commander to fill the trench, because they wanted to have proof and written orders so they could proceed in filling the trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and it's fairly easy to understand why, Colonel, because neither side wanted to fill in trenches without being absolutely certain that their senior command had ordered precisely that. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you say "neither side", I must say that during that period of time, and it did change later on, that the Muslims were definitely more anxious to fill in the trench than the Croat side. But as I said, it did change. As soon as the overall tactical situation changed in Central Bosnia, it was the other way around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and we'll get into that in just a second. But just continuing the escalation of tensions in April just before the outbreak of conflict, you gave some testimony about the kidnapping of four HVO staff officers, I believe, on April the 14th. The Court has already heard a lot of evidence about that. We don't need, really, very much more. But it was you who actually contacted the military authorities in Zenica to request that the incident be investigated; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Umm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's true that Mujahedin associated with the 7th Muslim Brigade were responsible for this incident, and you were not actually -- or your monitor, Mr. Baggesen, I believe, from whom we've heard, was not able to local the whereabouts of these four abducted HVO officers. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that, but I recall more or less my direct involvement with the HVO brigade commander, I think General Tadic, in Zenica, because I was directly involved in that one. And, yes, there was definitely links with the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next event that you spoke about in your direct examination was the Easter celebrations that you attended, the luncheon that you attended. I believe it's on April the 13th, at which Mr. Kordic was allegedly or was, in fact, present. Is there any reference in your notebook to the April 13th, 1993, Easter luncheon, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I was able to recall the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you actually speak to Mr. Kordic at that luncheon?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not sitting at his table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were lots of people there, I take it.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a head table, if my recollection is correct, and Mr. Kordic, along with Colonel Blaskic, were sitting at the head table. And the ECMM, since I was a brand new kid on the block, was sitting at one of the tables with other guests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that Ambassador Thebault was present at that --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the staff of the RC Zenica had been invited. Basically, the monitor with interpreters were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then you said that Mr. Kordic appeared in Travnik when there was an outbreak of tension or fighting there?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I say appeared, I must be very clear here, is that we went to Travnik because, as I depicted yesterday, tension has built up, different incidents took place, and they were all related or appear to have been initiated with this business of raising the Croat flag near the town hall, okay. And what we hand up is that as we were having this celebration, we received news that -- I don't recall exactly if it was from Travnik or if it was from BritBat, but that the situation has deteriorated to the point that BritBat was sending armoured vehicles there to try to calm down the situation. It seems to be out of control. And then we moved there and start meeting with different representative, local civilian police, military commanders, and then I recall very clearly that at the end of the day we almost had to hand up in the office of Mr. Kordic. And until then, I said that Mr. Kordic was in fact more or less working out of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you now understand that he was not working out of Travnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next event is the abduction of commander Zivko Totic on the morning of April 15th. You were aware that the four soldiers escorting him were executed?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see pictures of the car in which they had been travelling and their bodies aired on TV that day?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe not on TV, but what I did was that I went to the place where the incident took place. So I could see a trace of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you actually saw the car --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, that I recall that I have seen the car, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was riddled with bullets; a fairly graphic scene?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see a TV press conference given by members of the Croat leadership discussing this terrible incident in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because I must tell you that as soon as this incident took place, I was more or less given the special task to try to investigate and try to trace back the whereabouts of the Mujahedins that had in fact abducted General Totic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that at some point the Mujahedin, who had abducted Commander Totic and killed his escort, sent a letter to the ECMM threatening to kill people that they had in custody unless foreign nationals were released in Busovaca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me. None of this is disputed. The Prosecution doesn't dispute --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, I know. We are spending a lot of time on it. Why do we need to go through it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour. Let me move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that the fighting actually broke out in the Lasva Valley on the evening of April the 15th and not the morning of April the 16th, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- it took place definitely during that time, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You described your drive past Ahmici, sir. You do not know yourself whether the ABiH had a unit based in that village, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know if they had a unit in that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you do not know whether a specific defence plan existed for that village either, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that when I went and I had been given the chance, finally, to walk around, there was definitely no sign of defensive preparation on that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave some testimony, sir, that as you were driving along the valley road, from Vitez to Zenica on the 16th of April, you did not see any HVO troops. But let me just suggest to you that you were driving through HVO controlled territory and it's not surprising that you would not see any HVO troops, since the front lines were actually to the north of the supply route; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You meant HVO troops or you meant --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: HVO.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did say that I saw some HVO troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe we are talking at cross-purposes. You saw HVO troops, but you said you did not see any ABiH troops; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ABiH troops were located at the confrontation lines to the north of the village.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you agree, sir, that Ahmici was the only almost exclusively Muslim village behind the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. If you look at Vitez itself, there was Muslims in there too. So there was other small pockets of Muslims within the HVO controlled area, as there was pockets of HVO or Croats within Muslim territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were aware, were you not, that there had been an earlier incident in October of 1992, where a troop convoy was actually held up at Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Turning to Zenica, sir. It's true, is it not, that the two HVO brigades located in Zenica were militarily defeated on April the 16th and 17th?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say defeated, all I can say is that the battle took place, but my recollection is that some of them had been arrested. I visited them in the Zenica prison. But a lot of them too were able to withdraw and to escape and to more or less link up with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The long and the short of it is, though, that the HVO military presence no longer existed in Zenica as of April the 17th; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you yourself saw tank movements, I believe, around the Zenica environment by tanks owned by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, we reported one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. There was actually a April the 20th, 1993 report, which is already in evidence as 754, that refers to two tanks that were seen on the mountain road.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I thought you meant in Zenica, but the mountain road is not in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was one tank in Zenica and other tanks around the environs of Zenica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the fighting broke out, you made an attempt to contact Colonel Blaskic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were informed that he was not available?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you made no attempt to call Mr. Kordic, did you, or contact him in any way?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you are aware, no one else from BritBat attempted to contact Mr. Kordic that day, or thereafter?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I could not say, and I could not say either for Mr. Thebault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But no one in the ECMM, as far as you are aware, tried to contact Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I am not aware of what Mr. Thebault said. But all I said is that we try, okay, since we were working on the Busovaca Joint Commission and since the direct link that we had was Colonel Blaskic, I tried to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- establish contact with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were shown a document, sir, during your -- actually, you were shown two documents, both faxed, I believe, to the ECMM and to BritBat on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first was a document that had three signatures?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Signed by the same individual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Signed by the same individual?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just suggest to you that it was Mr. Anto Puljic who signed also for Mr. Ignac Kostroman, the Secretary-General of the HZ HB, and for Mr. Kordic, the vice-president of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Puljic?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name right now means nothing. Maybe I have met him. I don't know. I mean, you have to recall that those incidents took place several years ago, and my books are full of people that I have met. I would need to see his face, and then I could tell you if I've met him or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were aware that Mr. Kordic was the vice-president of the presidency of the HZ HB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. And he was located in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the fighting actually ceased as a result of -- from the Croat side as a result of orders issued by Mr. Mate Boban, and then by General Petkovic, and then by Colonel Blaskic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was eventually orders that were given, but I must tell you that at that time mainly through the military chain of command. So I know that -- I am aware that later on Petkovic came to Zenica or came to some other places, where finally Mr. Thebault was able to again get another ceasefire. And I must tell you that during that period there was many of those meeting. So I would not be able to recollect exactly when and at what meeting it took place, but I know that there was a series of meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We need not spend too much time on this, Colonel Landry, because these documents are already in evidence. But let me just suggest to you, since this is relatively important, from the chain of command perspective, that an order signed by both Mate Boban and President Izetbegovic --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- was signed on April the 18th, 1993. It's Exhibit D83/1. This order provided -- in fact, let's just put it on the ELMO. D83/1, please. If I might just ask the Court's direction, in order to save the Registrar a lot of work, we actually have clean copies of the exhibits that have previously been admitted into evidence. And it might be more efficient just to have the assistant put, or the usher, put these on the ELMO, Mr. President, if that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. These are two additional copies of the next two orders. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Colonel Landry, you would agree that President Izetbegovic and President Boban signed a four point order on the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Now that I have the document in front of me, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first paragraph provided that all misunderstandings in relations between Croatian and Muslim peoples in BH should be resolved by political means. Right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the fourth -- the third point, rather, was to -- an order to all units to stop the fighting immediately. Right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the fourth was to establish the responsibility and intentions of the units and individuals with a role at the beginning of the conflict. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next order I'd like you to examine is the order handed down the same day, sir, by the chief of the HVO main headquarters, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic. If you could just put that on the ELMO, please. And this order, as you would expect, sir, is sent by the commander in chief of the HVO military forces down to the various operative zones. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the way that the chain of command is normally expected to work? You would agree?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then the third order I'd like you to look at is an order of the same day signed by Colonel Blaskic, D84/1.
