And Colonel Blaskic, the operative zone commander, issues the same order that he had been instructed to issue by his commander in chief, his commanding officer. Right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So here you see a practical example of the chain of command in the HVO military working precisely as you would expect as a professional military man?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, after this series of orders had been issued, it's true that the warring factions got together in Zenica, they were assembled, I believe, by Lieutenant-General Morillon and by Ambassador Thebault, and an agreement was hammered out that day, April the 20th, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, yes. It could be another date, but I know that during that period there was many of those that took place, and I recall personally being involved with one that Morillon was chairing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We have previously had the document marked Exhibit D24/1, and the first provision of that agreement said, sir, that the BiH army, and the HVO, are both legal, military forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and are treated equally.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of that provision?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now that you are reading it, it definitely rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe the signatories to that are self-explanatory, Colonel. General Halilovic, who was the commander in chief of the ABiH armed forces, Brigadier Petkovic, commander in chief of the HVO forces, and countersigned by General Morillon and Ambassador Thebault. And you are familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at no point was Mr. Kordic involved in these negotiations. You would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No one suggested that his presentation was necessary in order to make any agreement relating to the cessation of hostilities binding; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as you are aware, no one from the ECMM invited him, no one from BritBat invited him? In fact, his name simply did not come up during the negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You are aware, Colonel, that notwithstanding this ceasefire agreement, hostilities continued sporadically in areas on the -- what had become the front lines? For example, in the village of Jelinak, a predominantly Croat village, the civilians were expelled by about a hundred BiH troops who -- consisted of a battalion sized grouping, and this was reported at the end of April of 1993. Do you have any recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any specific recollection. But as I am more than willing to admit, there has been retaliation on both sides and I am not trying to depict that one side was without fault. On the contrary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Turning to the next subject, which is the crimes against Croats that you investigated in the latter part of April and resulted in a special report that you prepared.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "latter part of April," you meant right after the mid-April incident?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was an imprecise phraseology on my part. It was actually your investigation that immediately preceded the special report on Croats in Zenica that you prepared, dated the 20th to the 21st of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's already in evidence, Your Honours, as the 25/1. As I understand it, sir, you were assisted by Father Stjepan Radic?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Known as Father Stjepan. That's all I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he reported to you that he had seen ABiH troops completely out of control, committing crimes, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it's what is written in the report, I would say yes. But to my knowledge, he didn't see that much because he was in central Zenica, okay. And what we did was that we took him with us, so that we could go and investigate the incident that took place on the villages which were bordering Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I don't think you are disagreeing with this, but you said in your testimony a couple of years ago, and it's been a few years, obviously, that Father Stjepan had given asylum to several Zenica HVO persons. This is page 7525 of the transcript. That they had seen the Bosnian troops were out of control, and it seemed --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people -- okay, that's what those people reported to Father Stjepan. And they were looking for asylum. And I've met those people, because I was then invited by Father Stjepan too. And those -- two individuals were politicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I think that I reported their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. As I understand it, sir, what you did was you conducted a two-day investigation. On the first day, you made a visit to the gaol in Zenica, where you saw hundreds of Croats incarcerated; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the second day you made a visit to various villages, and you reported your findings in this special report?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report, sir, you recite a fairly deplorable history of people being thrown out of their houses --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in Janjac?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stranjani?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Janjac, there were 209 families expelled from the village, that you record?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Stranjani, there were seven houses burned down and 240 other houses looted, all belonging to Croats, right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Zahalje, you found that four Croats had been murdered during the expulsion process?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The visit of Dobriljeno completely deserted of its Croat inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Zalje, you found 25 houses burned, the entire village deserted, ten civilians slaughtered, including one 90-year-old man and one three-year-old young girl, who had been shot dead in her bed. Right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If that's what I reported on my report, then that's exactly what we were told by the witnesses that were there in those village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone was ever brought to justice as a result of those atrocities?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You also investigated another incident that occurred a few days later in the village of Miletici, correct? April the 25th, I believe, where five people were tortured and murdered by ABiH Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it in the same report? Because this, I have no recollection. Unless it's on the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you to take a look at Exhibit D86/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we remain concerned about the relevance of this material which, as I understand it, wasn't dealt with in chief. And it's taking a lot of time to go through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a matter for us, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I did not mean to wander into material that was not covered on direct, but I believe that the crimes against Croats had in fact -- we can move on very briefly.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that I was not the one that did investigate this situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, sir, turning onto another subject. You gave some testimony about the relative strengths of the HVO military forces and the ABiH military forces, in your view. And you also gave some testimony today that the strategic and tactical situation changed during the midst of your tour of duty as an ECMM monitor. There is no question that as of the second or third week of April -- sorry, the second or third week of June, 1993, that the tide had most definitely turned against the HVO, and the ABiH forces were militarily dominant. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree. I mean, I would have to go through my notes to see exactly when it took place, but, yes, as I said earlier, yes, we could see that the whole tactical situation changed drastically in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that during the month of May and the first eight days of June of 1993, General Hadzihasanovic had resolutely refused to meet with Colonel Blaskic to discuss issues in a joint commission context? Did anyone tell you that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. Maybe I have been told, but I don't recall it. All I can say, though, is that I can recall that General Halilovic had been removed from his command later on and replaced by another general.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am about to move onto another subject. This might be a convenient time to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are you going to be very much longer, Mr. Sayers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would anticipate, Your Honour, as I said yesterday, I am not going to go beyond the morning session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How does that place us? I mean, you've had an hour and a half already, Mr. Sayers. You've got as far as Zenica. You are in the middle of April. There can't be very much more left to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There's the Zenica shelling, Your Honour; there is the Kiseljak testimony about which the witness spoke; there is the relative strengths of the ABiH and HVO forces in June, July, and August; the April the 28th convoy incident; and then the HV testimony that the witness gave. Those are the subjects that I would like to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, they should be dealt with in at least an hour, if not quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We have a witness who can be dealt with in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Nice. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We have a witness who can be dealt with in half a day, I'm sure. There's a short ex parte, if such a hearing can be granted, and there are various procedural matters that can usefully occupy any balance of the day, and particularly I know that exhibits have yet to be progressed. And there's the question of videos that I want to raise as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we can't sit late tonight. We shall have to adjourn very soon after four, so we may not be able to get very far with the other matter. But it does mean cross-examination should be expedited as quickly as possible. Yes, half past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's this map, Mr. Sayers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: We can address the point right now, Your Honour. The Colonel made a reference to a conversation that he had with General Praljak towards the end of his tour of duty, and General Praljak acknowledged the presence of HV troops around the town of Trebinje. This is a large relief or large-scale map of all of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia, and I just wanted the Colonel to point out exactly where Trebinje was for everybody's geographic reference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I missed part of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No problem. You gave some testimony about a conversation that you had had with General Praljak concerning the presence of HV troops in the town of Trebinje. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what else was I saying?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just would like you to point out where Trebinje is for everybody's easy reference, sir.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea, except that it has to be in the area of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For your assistance, sir, I've actually put a little yellow Post-It Note right below Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. This is not the type of map that we have used up there, so some of the names are not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would just look at the little yellow note, sir.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's many of those yellow --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, a yellow note.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There it is. Now, that's Trebinje. Would you just point it out for the three Judges, please?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right there [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the only point, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never been to that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Colonel, let me try to pick up the pace here a little, if I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave some very brief testimony about an incident on the 19th of April, 1993, in which Zenica, the city of Zenica, was shelled. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Look at your statement, on page 7. And I take it you've had the opportunity to review this statement at some point that you gave to the investigators four years ago.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me just suggest to you that you say that you made a record in your diary of the following: The first two rockets, you said, landed at about 12.10 hours. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is consistent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two more rockets landed in the city centre at 12.24?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then two others at 12.29?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two more rockets fell at 12.48, you said?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Umm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Umm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so that's a total of ten by now?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Umm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said further away from the town you heard two rockets hit at 13.56 hours?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two more at 14.04 hours, and earlier than that, two rounds of two rockets hit at 13.16 hours and two at 13.43 hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to go directly to my notes, but yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's a total of 18 rockets landing in Zenica or its environs in the space of about two hours, sir. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eighteen, you said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, I might have to go back to my note --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and then I'll give you a copy of exactly what I have here. The date again is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: April the 19th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm allowed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just so that we're agreed, sir, that's a total of 18 rockets landing in the city centre or in its environs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have six -- the six first ones, okay, were very near to Zenica. Okay, according to my note here, all the others were -- all I heard was a noise, and all I indicated here in my book was the fact that they landed far away, far away to the south, far away to the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I can give you a copy of my record here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Let me just ask the usher, if I may, to put page 7 of your statement on the ELMO. Let me just suggest to you, sir, that in the paragraph that's the second from the bottom, the chronology and the number of shells that I just went over with you is what appears in your statement.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that's exactly what I am saying, further away from the town, and then two fell to the south and north out of the town, and two -- and then two rockets were heard falling further away. So I am not referring to the fact that all those, except those six, shells fell into the city of Zenica. All I said is that my record says that they fell further away, outside of what we could observe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I counted then a total of 18, and you are saying that six rockets fell in the town centre, and so 12 would fall in the environs of Zenica, within two hours of the initiation of the shelling, or the rocket fire.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I have nine rounds, okay, besides those six that were -- that are heard that fell outside of Zenica. Okay. And then at 15.15, okay, we heard a very heavy machine gun firing within the city of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Six rounds inside the city and then a further nine outside of the city centre, is that right, for a total of 15 shells within a two-hour period?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12.24 to 14.04 hours, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few brief questions in connection with the testimony that you gave concerning your investigations of villages in the Kiseljak area, to the north of Kiseljak, sir. You did not find any dead bodies in Svinjarevo, Behrici, or Gomionica, did you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the people that signed the report, okay, I myself was the only one that did visit Rotilj. The other report was made by my counterpart, and I came, since I was responsible, I came to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you actually visit the villages of Svinjarevo, Behrici --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did visit the village of Rotilj, as I pointed out in my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I misunderstood that from your direct testimony, and I'm sorry for that. Let me turn to Rotilj. Did you ever speak to one of your co-monitors, Colonel Hendrik Morsink, about what had actually gone on at Rotilj, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell that he met the commander, Commander Mirko Redjo, R-e-d-j-o, who had led the assault on Rotilj after there had been firing from the village, and one of his soldiers had been killed?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection. But it could be possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just for the Trial Chamber's reference, I refer the Trial Chamber to pages 8220 and 8221 of Colonel Morsink's testimony. I am through with that subject. Next subject, sir. The question of whether the four HVO staff officers and Commander Totic had been abducted by Mujahedin was answered, wasn't it? There was no question, in your mind, that the Mujahedin were actually responsible for the abductions, and they were the people that actually gave up custody of these five people?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is that I definitely was involved with Totic, and there was no doubt in my mind that Totic had been abducted by Mujahedins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same thing is true of the four HVO officers; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I cannot refute or cannot confirm. All I know is that Totic was definitely kidnapped by Mujahedins, since I was myself directly involved with his release.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you prepare a contemporaneous record at the ECMM regarding the chronology of the events surrounding the release of these five HVO officers?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, to the best of my recollection, something was done with my good friend Dieter --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Schellschmidt?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dieter Schellschmidt. And we did prepare something at the end. Because he was working -- as I was working directly at Zenica, he was working, I think, at the -- in the military prison near Busovaca. I think. Because this operation was quite complicated when it was time to release the prisoners, and we had to work with BritBat, we had to work with ICRC, so we were quite split on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And Exhibit D79/1 is already in evidence. It was prepared by Mr. Schellschmidt. Did you actually witness yourself the circumstances that surrounded the coordinated release of the HVO prisoners and the ABiH prisoners, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've mentioned, I was the one coordinating this whole release from Zenica. And what was agreed was that, in Zenica, General Totic was supposed to be released there. And some other release or exchange of prisoner were taking place at the other place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you personally, sir, were -- there is no need to go over the report. It says what it says, so I'll move on. You were convinced that the Mujahedin had a special relationship with the 7th Muslim Brigade, which was under the direct control of the 3rd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know if it was a command relationship, but I definitely assumed throughout that they had some relationship.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it's right, sir, that Colonel Merdan, in particular, had close relations with the 7th Muslim Brigade; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my recollection, Merdan was the one that was having some kind of control over that brigade. And that's the reason why he was always escorting me when we were visiting the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Let me turn to the testimony that you gave regarding the April the 28th, 1993, UNHCR convoy incident. You would not disagree with the fact that incidents of this kind were breaking out, both in ABiH controlled territory and in HVO controlled territory, pretty regularly, right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. This was the first type of incident that any side, during my stay there, took control of an UNHCR convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who did you speak to on that day when you were in the office of your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. As I've told you, I was sitting at the ops centre while the meeting was going on in the conference room with Ambassador Thebault. I received a communication from BritBat, telling me that if the Croats were not to relieve the convoy, BritBat was to send a company or a squadron of warriors and they were going to get them out of there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, somebody from BritBat. Probably the ops officer from BritBat or maybe it was the commanding officer. I have no recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether you were speaking to someone who was actually a witness to the apprehension of the convoy itself, or were they merely --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that the guy with whom I was talking to was definitely somebody within the ops centre, because we were talking on the telephone. So that probably this individual was not the one that had physically witnessed what was going on. It had been reported to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What he was doing was reporting to you things that he had heard from other people, second or third hand, right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe not second or third hand, but I assume that if the ops centre had received this information, that before they start alarming the rest of the region, that they must have confirmed that in fact the UNHCR had been -- a convoy had been taken hostage. Because that's the normal procedures within military operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you yourself don't know whether that convoy had in fact been taken hostage, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no evidence, except the communication that I have and except for the fact that I did witness the argumentation that further on took place between Thebault, between Halilovic, and between Blaskic. Because that creates quite a turmoil at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the -- yes. One of the documents that you were shown yesterday, that we had not seen before, it was Exhibit Z857.3. I don't think there is any need to get it. The report says, "BHC report" -- this is paragraph C2 on page 2. "BHC report that on 28 April a 40-vehicle convoy, escorted by BritBat, was detained by HVO forces who demanded that they search it. HVO claim that their orders came from Mr. Kordic. They said they would ignore any orders from Colonel Blaskic or Brigadier Petkovic. Eventually Brigadier Petkovic contacted Mr. Kordic and the convoy was allowed to pass. The local HVO said they were only acting on Mr. Kordic's orders." You yourself do not know any of the details surrounding the interchange between the persons who were escorting the convoy or in the convoy and the HVO troops themselves, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know whether indeed those troops, whoever they were, the HVO forces, were indeed acting on Mr. Kordic's orders or not, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have to realise that the way that we -- the relationship that we've been having throughout that time with BritBat, okay, was a -- quite an extended relationship. We used to visit them on a regular basis, and I assume, based on previous incidents, that when something was reported to us through their own headquarters, that there was eventually obvious evidence that what they were telling us was the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself, sir, you do know, do you --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not. I was standing in the ops centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you never spoke to the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade, Mr. Grubesic, about this incident?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we felt we didn't have to. We had a commander right beside us and we had the army commander right beside us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's true, sir, that Ambassador Thebault, and the two commanders in chief of the warring forces, General Halilovic and Brigadier Petkovic, visited Busovaca the very next day, didn't they, April the 28th?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are not aware of anyone mentioning anything about this convoy, for example, to Commander Grubesic or to Mr. Kordic, are you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I recall, as I said, is that General Halilovic had to speak with him to diffuse the whole incident. And I don't know to whom he talked except that he was able to get somebody at the other end of the line which, for Thebault and myself, appeared to be Mr. Kordic, and eventually the whole convoy, the whole situation was defused. And then I assumed there must have been some links, some discussion that took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just follow this through a little bit in detail, sir. You don't know to whom Brigadier Petkovic actually spoke, do you, yourself?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why Mr. Brigadier Petkovic would have told me that he was talking to Mate Boban. I still recall that he said that he spoke to Mr. Kordic. I don't see why he would have lied to us. You have to realise that we were right now in the midst of trying to again come up with a ceasefire and that the HVO were trying to demonstrate to us that throughout there had been goodwill, and then this incident happened right in the midst of a kind of talk which we were to help out -- to defuse the whole situation, and I have this very clear knowledge. I put it in my report, and I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Colonel, I think we've got the point here. Now, Mr. Sayers, if you would like to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two points on this. Colonel Blaskic never stated that the -- to you at any point that the commander of the Busovaca Brigade was not entirely under his command, did he, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, following this incident, Colonel Blaskic reiterated to you and others that he was, in fact, the commander and chief of all the HVO troops in his territory?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he made that statement on several subsequent occasions, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, I believe in the Blaskic case, sir, two years ago, you said that this was obviously a misunderstanding between him and the political leaders, and happily the situation was peacefully corrected and resolved; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because otherwise some action would have been taken against Mr. -- the Busovaca Brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn to the month of June. It's true, isn't it, that the military attitudes on the part of the Muslim armed forces, in your view, hardened considerably in May of 1993 and thereafter and that the Muslim forces became far more aggressive, militarily?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, it could be early June, it could be mid-May. But, yes, in the course of my stay, we could see that there was a change in the relationship.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And there's no question, equally, that the ABiH launched large-scale offensives in June in Travnik and Kakanj simultaneously; is that right? You remember that, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember more the Kakanj thing. Okay, the Travnik, I would have to go again through my notes. But definitely Kakanj, because I was directly involved on numerous occasions to sign the ceasefire between the two of them in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree that these were large, well-organised offensives requiring advanced planning and logistical preparation; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, we've already heard from one senior representative of the ECMM that there were 20,000 refugees, Croat refugees, who had to leave the area as a result of the June offensive. That's Witness AD. Is that a number that's consistent with your recollection, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say, okay, but there was definitely refugees. So it could be 10,000, 20,000, or 30,000. I have no recollection of that number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Kakanj, where you were involved, is it your recollection that 10,000 refugees fled the city, Croat refugees, towards Vares?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have no recollection of the precise number, but, yes, definitely there were refugees that had to flee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any role in the ECMM's investigation or investigation by the United Nations Commission for Human Rights of atrocities committed during the Travnik offensive in June at Maljina and Cukle?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified that you paid visits on a regular basis to the BritBat headquarters. I'd just like to show you a BritBat military assessment of June the 9th, 1993, and ask you whether you agree with the conclusions contained in it. Thank you. I'd like to ask the usher to put the last page of this on the ELMO, page 10. It's the last one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This will be D194/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, the observation is made by the intelligence cell of the 1st Battalion of the Prince of Wales Own Regiment, in paragraph 7, that the June offensive was the first time that the BiH have taken the military initiative against the HVO in Central Bosnia. The milinfosum goes on to note that: "It would appear that Enver Hadzihasanovic and 3 Corps are orchestrating a carefully-planned and phased attack against the HVO in the areas of Travnik and the western Lasva Valley. In this context, Hadzihasanovic's constant refusals to meet Blaskic and his failure to attend negotiations concerning the situation in Travnik during that phase of the current fighting perhaps receive explanation." And the observation is made that the clearance of Travnik of all HVO elements was in a manner similar to that practiced in Zenica in April. Do you agree with those comments, sir, the military analysis of the BritBat in early June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is there a date on this document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: June the 9th, 1993, sir.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I would probably have phrased it slightly different, but, yes -- as I said, I would probably phrase it slightly different, but in essence, yes, I would tend to support this assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And then the milinfosum goes on to note, in paragraph 8, that: "The BiH have always been in the dominant military position in the Lasva Valley, and it now seems that they are prosecuting this advantage." The comment goes on to note that: "The timing of this action has probably been delayed by the issue of passage for the Convoy of Mercy." Do you agree with that military assessment, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would totally disagree with it, because I disagree with the first sentence, "The BiH have always been in the dominant military position in the Lasva Valley," as I disagree with this because that's not what I saw when I arrived there. And the reason, again, is that for the first few months that I was there, the Muslim -- excuse the expression -- but were more always walking on their knees to get -- to make sure that all agreements that they were doing with the Croats were to be fulfilled; i.e., roadblock, i.e., establishment of other necessities for their people, so I would disagree with that first sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Wouldn't you agree, though, that it was suicidal, under the circumstances, to route an aid convoy destined for Muslims in Tuzla directly through a war zone and HVO-held territory?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to correct what you said, because the Tuzla convoy was made up of Muslim and HVO Croats living in the Tuzla area, and if it would not have been for the force commander of the Tuzla -- the HVO force commander of the Tuzla area, probably this convoy situation would have ended up much more worse than the way it ended up. And if, again, you recall the Vance-Owen Plan that you've shown to me earlier, you would see that in it, okay, there is a paragraph stating that free access to the main road has to be provided, okay, to all the parties. And based on the willingness of all the parties to agree with the Vance-Owen Plan, and based on the willingness to all the commanders involved in the move of this Tuzla convoy, we agreed then to support the idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there's no question, sir, that the Tuzla convoy was driving up through Central Bosnia in the middle of a huge ABiH offensive against the HVO; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, it was not obvious that the major offensive of the BiH was that obvious, and then I would have challenged you. Then why was it accepted by the HVO to let it through, to let it go first? That's the judgement that I have right now, and that's, I recall very clearly, that Mr. Thebault, before launching this kind of initiative, had made sure that we had the support of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, sir, that the convoy took several days to wind its way up through Gornji Vakuf and Prozor, through Novi Travnik and into the Vitez area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right, as it took a lot of time too, to get through the port to start with, because it was stopped at different levels. As soon as the convoy passed Vitez on its way down, it was stopped on a regular basis, asking for more confirmation, more paperwork, and yet it was accepted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't have a clear recollection yourself of precisely when the ABiH offensive in the Travnik area was launched, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to go through all my paperwork. But all I can tell you is that all the resources of the ECMM were given to this convoy, so -- and I would tend to believe that if there would have been a major counterattack going on at that time, I'm sure that Mr. Thebault and some other upper staff of the ECMM would have more or less been involved in monitoring what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you this question, Colonel: Did you ever have any conversations with any representative of the 3rd Corps or the Muslim military command to make an inquiry why in the world a huge offensive would be launched just shortly before or pretty much simultaneously with the arrival of this large aid convoy right through HVO-held territory?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection. I was, on a regular basis, contacting the BiH, and I do not recall precisely asking that question or having a discussion on that specific issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear or see on television, sir, the consequences of an incident regarding a shell fired from Stari Vitez into Vitez during the evening of June the 10th, 1993, which literally blew eight small children to pieces?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it, but I have seen much atrocity on both sides; that I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But this was the evening before the convoy was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He doesn't recall it. I think we've probably exhausted this topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any dealings, Colonel, with the offensive launched -- offensives launched by the ABiH in the areas of Fojnica and Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there when it took place, but I definitely recall it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that the ABiH launched an attack on Fojnica on July the 3rd of 1993, one day after, I believe, Lieutenant-General Morillon had declared it to be a safe haven or a peace area, so-called? That's accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall it, because we totally disagreed with the evaluation of UNPROFOR regarding the future of Zenica, because we had warned them that eventually this was going to be the next target by BiH to secure their line of communication with Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your prediction turned out to be correct. Just one day after, they had been declared a peace area by UNPROFOR; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of that attack, a significant number of Croat refugees were expelled from their homes and left for the Vares area and Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would tend to agree with what you're saying, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. And similarly there was an all-out assault launched in the Bugojno area in July of 1993 which was successful, and resulted in the defeat of the HVO forces in that city and the usual sad tale of tens of thousands of refugees flooding out of the town for other Croat-held territory; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have no recollection of the number. It could be a few thousand, 10,000; that I cannot say. But, yes, usually after this kind of attack or this kind of situation, yes, it was always followed by a flood of refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just a few questions about Mr. Kordic. You knew that he held the post of vice-president of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I think you've already said that. But do you know what precisely -- what were the political powers that he was authorised to exercise? Did you ever have any conversations with him about that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never had any conversation. First of all, I must tell you that I never had a chance to visit him or to specifically have a chat with him, except for this incident in Travnik. But I came to realise very quickly that Mr. Kordic was more or less the overall political person responsible for the whole of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that there was not a damn thing which was taking place there which had a political objective which was not coming from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I think you said you only ever met him once; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you that I met him once, as far as having a meeting with him, but I met him on different other occasion, from a distance. For example, I met him on the Easter party. And maybe there is other -- a few other occasions where I was at the same location as he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you only ever recall one meeting with him, specifically?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the meeting that we had on the evening at Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet the president of the HVO, Dr. Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met a lot of people, but the name means nothing to me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet President Boban?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, on one very, very small occasion. And I meet some of the other people, as I have alluded to you earlier. As I became the deputy head -- before I became the deputy head, we went into the Mostar area, and I had a chance to meet with very high level figures within the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before you left the country, sir, on August the 24th, there was a meeting in Busovaca with ECMM representatives, where the chain of command was explained by Mr. Kordic; with General Praljak now as the commander in chief, General Petkovic as his chief of staff, and General Tole as the third in command. Do you recall that at all?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I recall, from what you said, is the fact that General Petkovic, for a reason not known to me, had been more or less -- had lost his appointment as commander in chief of the HVO forces. That is something very present to my memory. But that meeting, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just ask the usher to mark this as the next -- or the Registrar to mark this as one of the final exhibits. And we are coming to an end, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The exhibit is D195/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and the comment where it is reported by BritBat that Mr. Kordic, speaking with the ECMM in Busovaca on the 21st of August --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 3, sir, right at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where Mr. Kordic reiterates to ECMM in Busovaca, on the 21st of August, that Praljak was the senior commander, followed by Petkovic, and then Tole. Do you recall receiving a report by any of your subordinates at the ECMM regarding this meeting, or is this --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must tell you that this took place at a time that I was -- my last task at the ECMM, just prior to my departure, had been to prepare a special report on the Tuzla area. So I do not have a clear recollection of what took place during that period in Zenica. I could speak to you about Tuzla, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. Just a few miscellaneous subjects, and we'll wrap this up in about 15 minutes, I hope. You referred to some discussion that you had with the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, Colonel Merdan, and this was Exhibit Z719, where he articulated to you his view that there was some sort of a master plot against Muslims, and that they had proof that Mr. Kordic had supposedly met with Mr. Karadzic to discuss the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you recall that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, no evidence, let alone proof, was ever provided to you by Colonel Merdan of that; right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never saw any agreement or --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never saw any agreement that took place allegedly between Mate Boban and his counterpart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so, frankly, you simply have no idea whether there ever was such an agreement or not, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you probably are aware, one of the things that the monitors were doing was to report. And we, by reporting this kind of conversation -- and that's why in the report the name of Merdan is there -- is that we were just contributing through the whole knowledge of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I think I understand you. You are just reporting charges being made by one of the warring factions?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, it's true, is it not, that Colonel Blaskic, with whom you met on several occasions, he never told you that it was his aim to drive Muslims out of the Lasva Valley, did he? He never made any comments along those lines to you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He never made any disparaging comments about Muslims to you, did he, throughout the time that you --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he never told you that it was the policy of the HVO or the HDZ BiH to drive Muslims out of the Lasva Valley, did he?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except that we found it a bit awkward that following the incident in mid-April, then we started to receive all those -- all the communication coming up from the HVO to the fact that we should allow all the Croats in Zenica to move out of Zenica, because they were not well taken care of, which at that time was not really the case. Because, as you are probably aware, at that time, the Muslims were the only one, or the Bosniaks as they used to prefer to call themselves, were the only ones which were holding on all their minority, and doing and going at great lengths of effort not to allow them to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would concede, though, Colonel, wouldn't you, that the HVO had lost the military ability to protect Croats in the Zenica municipality as of April the 17th, 1993, when the two Zenica brigades were defeated there?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but I assume that that was not a reason why they had military forces in Zenica. I mean, their tasks were not to provide safety and security to the Croats and to Zenica; this was done by the joint police forces within Zenica. So whenever we had problems with the civilians in Zenica, I personally met the mayor and made sure that he was taking all the necessary steps to protect the Croat civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it perfectly logical, sir, that you would want people who were under your military protection to be in an area where you were able, militarily, to protect them?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. I couldn't agree more with you. The thing which we found a bit, though, annoying, is the fact that the date that those two requests came to us. I mean, we were still right in the middle of what we felt being still the fog of the war, and yet we receive this well-prepared letter, okay, telling us that you have to do something, our Croats are being massacred, and you must definitely make sure that they are being put on buses and brought back to us. My feeling would be that if I am in the middle of a military operation, than I would first of all try to find out what's going on in the military operation first. So that was the thing that we felt which was a bit annoying, the date at which we received this request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn to just another subject. You gave some testimony about an alleged agreement between President Milosevic and President Tudjman. I put it to you, Colonel Landry, that's just in the realm of scuttlebutt or gossip, isn't it? You never saw such an agreement and you don't know whether there was really such an agreement, do you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would tend to agree with you, with the exception that when it's becoming confirmed by all the International Community, and then it seems to that such a tacit agreement would not necessarily take place with a lot of publicity, but would be kept quite secret. But the fact of the matter was that it was well-known throughout UNPROFOR, throughout the ECMM, throughout Zagreb, that this had taken place. And the more incidents that we were seeing on the ground, as I've explained yesterday, the fact that the HVO brigade or the HVO forces that were in Tuzla were still cooperating with the Muslims, and yet we could not have the same kind of cooperation in Central Bosnia, was quite indicative to us that maybe that agreement had taken place and the borderline or the division line would be around Central Bosnia, between Serbs and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. This was the populous speculation that was going on in UNPROFOR and the ECMM. But the point I was making, sir, is that you never did find out that such an agreement had been concluded between those two heads of state, did you?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, do you have any knowledge if any disciplinary action was ever taken against ABiH soldiers responsible for the Totic kidnapping, the murders that we've seen in Zalje, and the other areas identified in your special report, in Miletici or in Maljina or Citluk?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall. Except the report that I made that I witnessed myself. As I was investigating the massacre that took place following those renewed combat operations in mid-April, that I witnessed a special unit within the BiH arresting people that were burglars and were not authorised to do so. Beside that, I have no recollection of what you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what ever happened to those people that were apprehended by the military police?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. With respect to the testimony regarding the Ahmici investigation that you gave, did you know that, in fact, Colonel Blaskic did order an investigation into the perpetrators of the Ahmici killings on the 10th of May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you agree, sir, that it would be hard for him to -- or hard for the Croats to conduct that investigation without being able to identify eyewitnesses to the actual events on that day, April the 16th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think that's very helpful. It's a pure matter of comment, which you can make to us in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'll move onto my final subject, Mr. President, and I hope to be through by 12.30, as I undertook to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe, sir, that because of the rumours of the presence of HV troops in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you insisted that specific observations be made, and that if there were indeed HV troops, they should be identified, and a special effort to do so should be undertaken; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a lot of pressure from HQ Zagreb to try to come up with identification of units that were in that area. And as I said yesterday, I personally witnessed, okay, HV equipment, military equipment in the area of Prozor, which was then -- further other ECMM monitors did see the same thing. And later on, one of the HV commanders did say that there was HV equipment --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to interrupt you, and I don't mean to be discourteous, sir. But the question was: It's true that you instructed your monitors, having received instructions from your superiors, to undertake a special effort to identify HV troops in Bosnia. Right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because the allegation was serious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And, in fact, you were asked to be very careful, to try to verify, whenever you came across a military convoy, to verify that it was indeed a HV convoy; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you would agree that it was difficult to identify HV units, because, as you've speculated, most of the movement must have been carried out at night. Right?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that accounts for the sporadic, intermittent sightings of allegedly HV troops, or at least vehicles bearing HV marks; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir. They were not allegedly. I mean, I would not see the reason why HVO logistic vehicles would bear the mark of HV. I mean, it would be totally going against the whole strategy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never saw any fighting units anywhere in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw any fighting units. Because we were not allowed, as I said, to go to some of the places where those fightings involving HVO -- HV forces were taking place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You never gained any information, with all of your -- all of the resources available to you, that HV forces were in fact controlled -- HV forces controlled the HVO, did you? In other words, dictated --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was never any information that you came across to the effect that the HV controlled the military policy or strategy of the HVO, was there?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received that information. Mind you, we had some doubt about it, but it was just speculation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You never saw any HV troops yourself in the Vitez-Busovaca pocket, in Kiseljak, in Zepce, Vares?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never saw any in Central Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never received any reports of any HV troops present in any of the municipalities that I've just identified, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Central Bosnia, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only logistics units you saw were south of Prozor and --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the Prozor area, but not south of Prozor; in the Prozor area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All of those were outside of the area of responsibility of Colonel Blaskic, not within the Central Bosnia operative zone, as far as you are aware; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel, thank you very much indeed. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. No, there is not any questions. Re-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance quickly, please, to hand the witness all at the same time 603, 609, 636, 639.1, 724.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that these documents are the ones that we discussed yesterday that were not admitted, because they had not been provided to us, and weren't tendered during the direct examination, so far as I am aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Two are, Your Honour, two are not, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The two that were not can't be put to the witness. You can put those that were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, while that's being done, allow me to point out to the Court, on 639.1 and on 724.2, the two ECMM documents from Canada, that the Defence has raised in cross-examination a suggestion that ECMM was not aware of an ultimatum that can be used for Mr. Boban. Both those documents contemporaneous with the time of when this was happening indicate exactly that there was awareness of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We have the point. There is no need to take it any further. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In that spirit, Your Honour -- I won't take the usher's time further than with 603, 609, and 636, except again, Your Honour, if the Court will allow me to indicate these are three press articles contemporaneous with the time from various, I would think, generally respectable sources, April 4th, April 5th, and the 10th of April, all reporting the fact of this ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning with that background, Colonel, if you could look briefly, if you still have it in front of you, to the document tendered to you by the Defence, D83/1. If you don't have it, I can hand it to you. If we have an extra copy, perhaps we can do it more quickly. Do you have that, sir? This was the document put before you by Mr. Sayers a few minutes ago. Well, no, I'm sorry, not -- it's not the correct document. Perhaps we could move forward this way. There was a document shown to you, signed by Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban, dated the 18th of April, 1993, about a peace settlement, if you will. Do you recall that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that it was shown to me earlier, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, you don't have that document at the podium?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it would assist, I have a copy here for counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If the Defence have it, it could be passed on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise for the delay, Your Honour. Two very short questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This agreement, dated the 18th of April, 1993, this was, in fact, by its date, after HVO attacks in Central Bosnia, the Lasva Valley, and elsewhere on the 16th and 17th of April, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And assuming for the moment, for the record, that there was one, after the April 15th deadline passed; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, this agreement, this peace agreement, was signed apparently in Zagreb. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In terms of the Convoy of Joy, the timing of that, could I again ask the witness to be shown what was put before him a moment ago? I believe it was 194/1, the milinfosum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could direct your attention to the second page, the item numbered "8". If I can direct your attention --

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say page 2?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 2, item 8. I hope we're looking at the same document. If you can see it -- and your copy is rather poor, I suppose -- well, let me see. On item 8, starting with the second line of -- second sentence of paragraph 8, in reference to the BiH offensive, it says -- the document says: "The timing of this action has probably been delayed by the issue of passage for the Convoy of Mercy and its significance in the context of a starving Tuzla area. Military action in the Lasva Valley effectively cut the only remaining route to the north. The delays that this convoy has met with en route may have finally convinced 3 Corps that prospect for its arrival in the north are slim and that accordingly they should restrain themselves no longer." In reference to the questions asked of you by Mr. Sayers, does this indicate, sir, that in fact this offensive did not take place or was not a mission until after the Convoy of Joy?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would tend to agree with your assessment, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning the Zenica shelling, you used in your accounts -- in the questions that Mr. Sayers put to you, you used the word "rockets" as opposed to using the word "shell". Is there any significance to you in terms of the fact that you had at one point -- at one time the word "rocket" was used in terms of the shells that fell, excuse me, in the centre of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that I used the term "rocket".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know or did you know, in fact -- did you actually go out and investigate the craters or the shelling, other than what you heard from your hotel room?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I heard and later on from what we reported, somebody else did make the investigation for that specific incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who -- the question came up, you said there was a senior HVO official who you spoke with in Mostar in May or June of 1993 about the Vance-Owen Plan. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection. I would have to go through my notes to find out exactly with whom I met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection as to what he said about the Vance-Owen Plan at that time?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look at my notes, so I have no recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. I'm not going to ask you to do that, Colonel. Concerning the UNHCR convoy, you were present when Colonel Blaskic and General Petkovic were there trying to sort this situation out?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, because they needed the communications which were in my office at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say anything to you or was it interpreted to you that there was anything that cast any doubt that these events were, in fact, taking place as they spoke in the way that you've described them to the Court?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I said that this led me to believe that what had been reported to us was what, in fact, was going on at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no report -- indication from Colonel Blaskic or General Petkovic to you that these events, in fact, were not taking place?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm almost completed, Your Honour. I'm just looking through my various notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning the Vance-Owen Plan, the questions asked you by Mr. Sayers, did it appear to you that what the -- under their interpretation of the Vance-Owen Plan, what the Bosnian Croats appeared to have in mind was something more homogeneously Croat than what the Vance-Owen Plan provided for, as you and ECMM understood it?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on the incident that took place, based on the way that the situation was developing in Central Bosnia, yes, that's what we tend to agree on within RC Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have about two questions, Your Honour, and I'll be completed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the Vance-Owen Plan, the annex that Mr. Sayers pointed you to and the make-up of the Travnik government, under this plan the governor would have been Croat, the vice-governor would have been Muslim or Bosniak, and of the other members, the Muslims would have had only one less -- only one less than the Croats in making up that government; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what you saw and were informed about on the ground, Colonel, did such a composition as just outlined -- did that appear to you to be acceptable to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: REMI LANDRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that I cannot comment on it, but all I can say is that my recollection tells me that that never eventually materialised as it was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Colonel, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next witness is ready, and Mr. Lopez-Terres will deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, we've seen the summary of this witness. She clearly went through a terrible time. You can take that part of the evidence, I'm sure, fairly shortly --

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- so as not to distress her. Obviously, the evidence on page 2 is the significant part and, of course, you could take longer with that. I would say as far as cross-examination is concerned, as I said with an earlier witness who gave evidence about events which she was directly involved in, distressing events, we should not expect you to cross-examine at any length, and you won't be criticised for not doing so. I would add this: that if as a result of that the cross-examination is short, I don't regard that as a criticism of the Defence, and I hope nobody else will criticise them, for handling the witness here, if they have constraint in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If we may suggest which paragraphs should not be led by leading questions, 21, 25, and 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And speaking for Mr. Kordic, we would appreciate it if the Prosecution would not lead paragraphs 8 through 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you would like to take a seat. Examined by Mr. Lopez-Terres:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you Mrs. Nura Mujanovic, widow of Mr. Sefik Pezer, and were you born in 1948 in the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1993, you lived with your family, that is, your late husband, Sefik Pezer of 52 years of age, your son, Ahmed Pezer, who was 27, and your two daughters, Alma and Taiba, 20 and 15, your daughter-in-law and your granddaughter, in a house that you owned in Zume, that is, in the lower part of Ahmici, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes, that was my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Zume, there were some 35 houses lived in by Muslims, but the majority of inhabitants of the village were Croats, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your husband, Sefik, and your son, Ahmed, were both members of the Zume Village Territorial Defence, and as such, stood guard, that is, participated in night shifts of the guards in the village?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they had only one weapon, and that was an old hunting rifle, a rifle which belonged to the father of your husband, Sefik?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croat villagers knew that your husband and your son had that weapon, because they returned so when they stood guard in the village jointly?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the afternoon of the 15th of April, 1993, you and your husband went to visit your cousin, who lived at Krcevine and whose son, by the name of Emir, had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your husband's cousin confirmed to you that Emir had indeed been arrested with some other Muslims at a time when he was going to the Bratstvo Factory in Novi Travnik to work, and that that particular arrest, that a bus had been intercepted at a place called Stojkovici; is that so?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes. That is where they separated the Muslims and arrested them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you went to visit your cousin, did you watch television on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NURA PEZER
utterances.text: Yes. It was the afternoon news and we watched it, and Dario Kordic appeared in the news, and Tihomir Blaskic was present. And he said, "My combatants are ready. They are waiting for the orders." But we did not think that anything would happen. We did not simply think that anything would happen, and we stayed there for a little while and then went back home to Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
